concerns.text: Task T012 restricts human sample selection to 'the most recent commits per repo' (1 sample), directly contradicting Spec FR-001 and Plan 'Balanced Blocked Design' which mandate '3 samples per repository' to achieve N=150. This is a semantic weakening of the data collection requirement.

Spec FR-005 mandates the pipeline 'halts' if the tool false positive rate exceeds the threshold. Task T014 explicitly instructs 'Do not impose a hard threshold... simply report,' and Task T023 only 'flags' the status without implementing the required halt mechanism. This drops a critical acceptance criterion.

Task T028 restricts the sensitivity analysis sweep to the 'Long Method' threshold only. Spec FR-008 and US-3 require sensitivity analysis on thresholds for *all* four code smell categories to ensure robustness. This is a silent narrowing of the statistical analysis scope.

Task T012.5 assumes 50 tasks derived from human issues, but T012 only extracts metadata for 1 function per repo (50 repos). The Plan requires 150 LLM samples (3 per task). The task description fails to specify how to derive 50 distinct tasks from 50 repos to support the 3x replication required by the Balanced Blocked Design, risking a data mismatch.

Task T022.5 proposes 'creating' a clean reference set or fetching a 'verified subset' without specifying checksumming or derivation logs. This risks violating Constitution Principle III (Data Hygiene) which requires all data under `data/` to be checksummed and derivations documented.
